content.content:
1	# frame-codec
2	
3	Binary frame codec for a length-prefixed wire format, with a checksum, a version byte and precise errors for truncated or damaged input.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	Go 1.22 or newer. Standard library only.
8	
9	## Build
10	
11	    go build ./...
12	    go run ./cmd/framedecode --file <path>
13	
14	## Public interface
15	
16	`codec.Encode(frame Frame) ([]byte, error)` returns the framed bytes.
17	- `codec.Decode(data []byte) (Frame, error)` returns the decoded frame.
18	- `type Frame struct { Version uint8; Flags uint16; Kind uint8; Payload []byte }`.
19	- `codec.HeaderSize`, `codec.MaxPayload` constants.
20	- `codec.ErrShortFrame`, `codec.ErrBadVersion`, `codec.ErrChecksum`, `codec.ErrTooLarge` error values.
21	
22	## Multi-frame sessions
23	
24	`codec.NewSession(w io.Writer, r io.Reader) *Session` wraps one byte
25	writer and one byte reader in a concurrency-safe session. Frames are
26	just concatenated single-frame encodings, so the wire format and the
27	single-frame entries are unchanged.
28	
29	- `(*Session).WriteFrame(Frame) error` appends one whole encoded frame
30	  in call-arrival order; an oversized payload returns `ErrTooLarge`
31	  before any byte is buffered.
32	- `(*Session).Flush() error` writes everything buffered so far to the
33	  underlying writer (and flushes it when it implements `Flush` itself).
34	- `(*Session).ReadFrame() (Frame, error)` parses incrementally: complete
35	  frames are returned one per call while a trailing half frame stays
36	  buffered for later bytes. A clean end of input returns `io.EOF`; a
37	  truncated trailing frame returns `ErrShortFrame`; a corrupt frame
38	  returns the same value `Decode` would return for it and stops further
39	  delivery, with previously returned frames already in the caller's
40	  hands.
41	
42	Reads and writes are independently serialized, so one session may be
43	shared by concurrent writers and readers; the bytes of a single frame
44	are never interleaved.
45	
46	## Reliable sessions
47	
48	`codec.NewReliable(sess *Session, cfg ReliableConfig) (*ReliableSession, error)`
49	wraps an existing session in a reliability layer. The lower wire format
50	is not changed: every reliable message is the payload of one ordinary
51	codec frame, prefixed by this layer's own envelope, so `Encode`/`Decode`,
52	the header constants and the four established error values keep their
53	exact byte-level semantics.
54	
55	- `ReliableConfig{Window int; StateDir string}`: send/receive window
56	  width in frames and a directory for write-side state (checkpoint and
57	  replay log); it is created if missing.
58	- `ReliableFrame{Flags uint16; Kind uint8; Payload []byte}` is the
59	  caller-visible frame. `EnvelopeSize` (16) bytes are reserved inside
60	  the underlying frame, so the inner payload limit is
61	  `ReliableMaxPayload = MaxPayload - EnvelopeSize`.
62	- `(*ReliableSession).WriteFrame(ReliableFrame) error` numbers frames in
63	  write order, journals each one, and parks it in the send window;
64	  nothing goes out before `Flush`. When the window is full it returns
65	  the established over-limit value `ErrWindowFull` (the same sentinel as
66	  `ErrTooLarge`) and drops the frame without consuming a sequence. An
67	  oversized inner payload returns `ErrTooLarge`.
68	- `(*ReliableSession).Flush() error` sends all windowed frames in seq
69	  order, each piggybacking a cumulative "next expected" acknowledgement,
70	  plus one pure ack; on a restart the window is reloaded from the replay
71	  log, so `Flush` is also the retransmit operation.
72	- `(*ReliableSession).ReadFrame() (ReliableFrame, error)` delivers in seq
73	  order exactly once. Acks advance the send window; duplicates of
74	  delivered or parked frames are re-acknowledged but never redelivered;
75	  in-window out-of-order frames are parked and delivered as a contiguous
76	  run once the gap closes; a declared sequence outside the window's
77	  reach (an ancient residual older than one window width, or one width
78	  ahead of the current position) is refused with `ErrChecksum`, stopping
79	  delivery stickily at the current position. Outer-layer results
80	  (`io.EOF`, `ErrShortFrame`, outer checksum/version/size errors) pass
81	  through unchanged.
82	
83	Standalone acks are written by a small background pump, so a writer
84	that needs the peer's acks to drain its window must let `ReadFrame` run
85	(or run it in a dedicated goroutine for one-directional traffic).
86	
87	### Crash recovery
88	
89	Written data frames are recorded in a CRC'd replay log (`reliable.log`);
90	the acknowledged position is recorded in a dual-slot checkpoint
91	(`reliable.ckp`), writing the alternate slot with a higher generation
92	each time:
93	
94	- a checkpoint torn by a crash mid-write fails its own CRC and is
95	  ignored, falling back to the previous complete record;
96	- a truncated replay log, or a flipped bit in a complete record, fails
97	  recovery with `ErrChecksum` rather than delivering unverified frames;
98	- the checkpoint is made durable before the log prefix is discarded, so
99	  reconciliation always resumes from the earlier confirmed position: no
100	  acknowledged frame is resent past the peer's state, no unacknowledged
101	  frame is skipped, and the receiver deduplicates the overlap.
102	
103	After recovery the first `Flush` re-sends every frame past the resume
104	point; backlogs wider than the window drain as acks refill the freed
105	tail slots from the log.
106	
107	## Channel multiplexing
108	
109	`codec.NewMux(rel *ReliableSession, cfg MuxConfig) (*Mux, error)`
110	carries several independent logical channels over one reliable
111	session. The lower wire format is not changed: every multiplexed
112	message is the payload of one reliable data frame, prefixed by this
113	layer's own 15-byte header
114	(`chan uint16`, `seq uint32`, `flags uint8`, `ack uint32`, `crc32`),
115	so the reliable envelope, the codec frame, the header constants and
116	all established error values keep their exact semantics.
117	
118	- `MuxConfig{Channels int; Window int; StateDir string}`: the number of
119	  channels (numbered `0..Channels-1`), the per-channel in-flight quota
120	  in frames (enforced independently), and a write-side state directory
121	  (per-channel dual-slot checkpoints, a shared replay journal and
122	  per-channel close markers), created if missing.
123	- `ChannelFrame{Channel uint16; Flags uint16; Kind uint8; Payload []byte}`
124	  is the caller-visible frame. `MuxHeaderSize` (15) bytes are reserved
125	  inside the reliable payload, so the inner payload limit is
126	  `MuxMaxPayload = ReliableMaxPayload - MuxHeaderSize`.
127	- `(*Mux).WriteFrame(ChannelFrame) error` numbers frames per channel in
128	  write order, journals each one and parks it in the channel's quota;
129	  nothing goes out before `Flush`. A full per-channel quota returns the
130	  established over-limit sentinel `ErrWindowFull` (the same value as
131	  `ErrTooLarge`); an oversized payload returns `ErrTooLarge`. A rejected
132	  frame is neither queued nor journaled and consumes no sequence, so it
133	  takes no quota; total buffering is bounded by `Channels*Window`.
134	  Writing to a closed channel returns the new sentinel
135	  `ErrChannelClosed`; an out-of-range channel returns `ErrChecksum`.
136	- `(*Mux).CloseChannel(ch) error` closes one channel's write side: the
137	  FIN is itself a sequence entry (it takes one quota slot, so a full
138	  quota gives `ErrWindowFull` and the close is retried after acks); a
139	  channel that was never written is opened first, so an unused channel
140	  still delivers a clean EOF. Closing or writing an already closed
141	  channel returns `ErrChannelClosed`.
142	- `(*Mux).Flush() error` sends queued frames round-robin across
143	  channels (each pass serves at most one queued frame per channel,
144	  starting where the previous Flush stopped), so one busy channel can
145	  never starve another and a channel's frames never pass its own
146	  earlier frames. Every frame piggybacks the sender's current
147	  cumulative receive position for its channel; cumulative
148	  acknowledgements are also sent by a small background pump. As on the
149	  reliable layer, a writer that needs the peer's acks to drain quotas
150	  must let `ReadFrame` run.
151	- `(*Mux).ReadFrame() (ChannelFrame, error)` delivers across all
152	  channels: a gap-blocked channel never stalls another channel, while
153	  within a channel frames arrive in write order exactly once. After a
154	  channel's remaining frames, the read that reaches its FIN returns the
155	  `ChannelFrame` naming the channel together with `io.EOF`; other
156	  channels keep flowing. A channel number outside the session's reach,
157	  a residual older than one channel-window, a declaration more than one
158	  window ahead, an acknowledgement past the send frontier, a
159	  same-sequence retransmission with different content, an unknown flag,
160	  an ack carrying payload, or a damaged header is refused with
161	  `ErrChecksum`, stopping stickily at the current delivery positions.
162	  Reliable-layer results (`io.EOF`, `ErrShortFrame`, outer
163	  checksum/version/size and reader errors) pass through unchanged; when
164	  a terminal lower-layer read also brings complete frames, the buffered
165	  frames are delivered first.
166	
167	Restart uses the same durable rules as the reliable layer: written data
168	frames are CRC-recorded in a shared journal (`mux.log`), acknowledged
169	per-channel positions in dual-slot checkpoints (`muxNNN.ckp`), and a
170	close marker (`muxNNN.closed`) survives a FIN whose journal prefix was
171	discarded. Recovery resumes each channel at the earlier of the
172	checkpoint and journal positions, so no unacknowledged frame is skipped
173	and the receiver deduplicates the overlap; a truncated journal or a
174	flipped bit in a complete record fails recovery with `ErrChecksum`. If
175	the close marker cannot be written, the close still takes effect: the
176	FIN is already journaled, so the in-memory state and the journal stay
177	consistent and a later restart recovers the same closed channel.
178	
179	## Fragmentation and reassembly
180	
181	`codec.NewFrag(m *Mux, cfg FragConfig) (*FragSession, error)` carries
182	whole payloads larger than the single-frame limit over one multiplexed
183	session: the caller writes each complete payload once and this layer
184	cuts it into ordered fragments that ride ordinary mux frames, so the
185	mux header, the reliable envelope, the codec frame, the header
186	constants and all established error values keep their exact semantics.
187	The fragment header lives only inside the mux payload
188	(`msg uint32`, `idx uint32`, `total uint32`, `flags uint8`,
189	`ack uint32`, `crc32`); no new error values are introduced.
190	
191	- `FragConfig{MaxMessage int; StateDir string}`: the per-channel
192	  reassembly cap in bytes (no message may declare more) and a directory
193	  for the per-channel reassembly state files, created if missing.
194	- `FragFrame{Channel uint16; Flags uint16; Kind uint8; Payload []byte}`
195	  is the caller-visible message. `FragHeaderSize` (21) bytes are
196	  reserved inside the mux payload, so one fragment carries at most
197	  `FragMaxPayload = MuxMaxPayload - FragHeaderSize` chunk bytes.
198	- `(*FragSession).WriteFrame(FragFrame) error` slices the payload into
199	  ordered fragments and queues every fragment of the message
200	  atomically, so two messages of one channel never interleave; nothing
201	  goes out before `Flush`. A payload larger than `MaxMessage` returns
202	  `ErrTooLarge`; a channel whose in-flight quota is already exhausted
203	  returns `ErrWindowFull` (the same value as `ErrTooLarge`); both drop
204	  the write without consuming a message or frame sequence, so a
205	  rejected payload takes no buffer. Writing to a closed channel returns
206	  `ErrChannelClosed`; an out-of-range channel returns `ErrChecksum`.
207	- `(*FragSession).Flush() error` is the mux flush: fragments go out
208	  round-robin across channels, so one channel's fragments may be
209	  interleaved with other channels' frames, and a message whose
210	  fragments span several windows drains as acknowledgements arrive.
211	- `(*FragSession).ReadFrame() (FragFrame, error)` delivers one
212	  reassembled message per call, exactly once, with byte content and
213	  call order identical to the writes; a message stalled mid-assembly on
214	  one channel never blocks another channel's delivery. A fragment whose
215	  declared total exceeds the reassembly cap drops its whole message
216	  with `ErrTooLarge` and the stream continues. A fragment from an old
217	  message generation, one beyond the current receive position, a
218	  same-position duplicate with different content, an acknowledgement
219	  past the send frontier, an unknown flag, a malformed standalone
220	  acknowledgement, or a damaged fragment header is refused with
221	  `ErrChecksum` - the bare established value, comparable directly with
222	  `==` - and stops delivery stickily at the current position. Mux

# frame-codec

Binary frame codec for a length-prefixed wire format, with a checksum, a version byte and precise errors for truncated or damaged input.

## Requirements

Go 1.22 or newer. Standard library only.

## Build

    go build ./...
    go run ./cmd/framedecode --file <path>

## Public interface

`codec.Encode(frame Frame) ([]byte, error)` returns the framed bytes.
- `codec.Decode(data []byte) (Frame, error)` returns the decoded frame.
- `type Frame struct { Version uint8; Flags uint16; Kind uint8; Payload []byte }`.
- `codec.HeaderSize`, `codec.MaxPayload` constants.
- `codec.ErrShortFrame`, `codec.ErrBadVersion`, `codec.ErrChecksum`, `codec.ErrTooLarge` error values.

## Multi-frame sessions

`codec.NewSession(w io.Writer, r io.Reader) *Session` wraps one byte
writer and one byte reader in a concurrency-safe session. Frames are
just concatenated single-frame encodings, so the wire format and the
single-frame entries are unchanged.

- `(*Session).WriteFrame(Frame) error` appends one whole encoded frame
  in call-arrival order; an oversized payload returns `ErrTooLarge`
  before any byte is buffered.
- `(*Session).Flush() error` writes everything buffered so far to the
  underlying writer (and flushes it when it implements `Flush` itself).
- `(*Session).ReadFrame() (Frame, error)` parses incrementally: complete
  frames are returned one per call while a trailing half frame stays
  buffered for later bytes. A clean end of input returns `io.EOF`; a
  truncated trailing frame returns `ErrShortFrame`; a corrupt frame
  returns the same value `Decode` would return for it and stops further
  delivery, with previously returned frames already in the caller's
  hands.

Reads and writes are independently serialized, so one session may be
shared by concurrent writers and readers; the bytes of a single frame
are never interleaved.

## Reliable sessions

`codec.NewReliable(sess *Session, cfg ReliableConfig) (*ReliableSession, error)`
wraps an existing session in a reliability layer. The lower wire format
is not changed: every reliable message is the payload of one ordinary
codec frame, prefixed by this layer's own envelope, so `Encode`/`Decode`,
the header constants and the four established error values keep their
exact byte-level semantics.

- `ReliableConfig{Window int; StateDir string}`: send/receive window
  width in frames and a directory for write-side state (checkpoint and
  replay log); it is created if missing.
- `ReliableFrame{Flags uint16; Kind uint8; Payload []byte}` is the
  caller-visible frame. `EnvelopeSize` (16) bytes are reserved inside
  the underlying frame, so the inner payload limit is
  `ReliableMaxPayload = MaxPayload - EnvelopeSize`.
- `(*ReliableSession).WriteFrame(ReliableFrame) error` numbers frames in
  write order, journals each one, and parks it in the send window;
  nothing goes out before `Flush`. When the window is full it returns
  the established over-limit value `ErrWindowFull` (the same sentinel as
  `ErrTooLarge`) and drops the frame without consuming a sequence. An
  oversized inner payload returns `ErrTooLarge`.
- `(*ReliableSession).Flush() error` sends all windowed frames in seq
  order, each piggybacking a cumulative "next expected" acknowledgement,
  plus one pure ack; on a restart the window is reloaded from the replay
  log, so `Flush` is also the retransmit operation.
- `(*ReliableSession).ReadFrame() (ReliableFrame, error)` delivers in seq
  order exactly once. Acks advance the send window; duplicates of
  delivered or parked frames are re-acknowledged but never redelivered;
  in-window out-of-order frames are parked and delivered as a contiguous
  run once the gap closes; a declared sequence outside the window's
  reach (an ancient residual older than one window width, or one width
  ahead of the current position) is refused with `ErrChecksum`, stopping
  delivery stickily at the current position. Outer-layer results
  (`io.EOF`, `ErrShortFrame`, outer checksum/version/size errors) pass
  through unchanged.

Standalone acks are written by a small background pump, so a writer
that needs the peer's acks to drain its window must let `ReadFrame` run
(or run it in a dedicated goroutine for one-directional traffic).

### Crash recovery

Written data frames are recorded in a CRC'd replay log (`reliable.log`);
the acknowledged position is recorded in a dual-slot checkpoint
(`reliable.ckp`), writing the alternate slot with a higher generation
each time:

- a checkpoint torn by a crash mid-write fails its own CRC and is
  ignored, falling back to the previous complete record;
- a truncated replay log, or a flipped bit in a complete record, fails
  recovery with `ErrChecksum` rather than delivering unverified frames;
- the checkpoint is made durable before the log prefix is discarded, so
  reconciliation always resumes from the earlier confirmed position: no
  acknowledged frame is resent past the peer's state, no unacknowledged
  frame is skipped, and the receiver deduplicates the overlap.

After recovery the first `Flush` re-sends every frame past the resume
point; backlogs wider than the window drain as acks refill the freed
tail slots from the log.

## Channel multiplexing

`codec.NewMux(rel *ReliableSession, cfg MuxConfig) (*Mux, error)`
carries several independent logical channels over one reliable
session. The lower wire format is not changed: every multiplexed
message is the payload of one reliable data frame, prefixed by this
layer's own 15-byte header
(`chan uint16`, `seq uint32`, `flags uint8`, `ack uint32`, `crc32`),
so the reliable envelope, the codec frame, the header constants and
all established error values keep their exact semantics.

- `MuxConfig{Channels int; Window int; StateDir string}`: the number of
  channels (numbered `0..Channels-1`), the per-channel in-flight quota
  in frames (enforced independently), and a write-side state directory
  (per-channel dual-slot checkpoints, a shared replay journal and
  per-channel close markers), created if missing.
- `ChannelFrame{Channel uint16; Flags uint16; Kind uint8; Payload []byte}`
  is the caller-visible frame. `MuxHeaderSize` (15) bytes are reserved
  inside the reliable payload, so the inner payload limit is
  `MuxMaxPayload = ReliableMaxPayload - MuxHeaderSize`.
- `(*Mux).WriteFrame(ChannelFrame) error` numbers frames per channel in
  write order, journals each one and parks it in the channel's quota;
  nothing goes out before `Flush`. A full per-channel quota returns the
  established over-limit sentinel `ErrWindowFull` (the same value as
  `ErrTooLarge`); an oversized payload returns `ErrTooLarge`. A rejected
  frame is neither queued nor journaled and consumes no sequence, so it
  takes no quota; total buffering is bounded by `Channels*Window`.
  Writing to a closed channel returns the new sentinel
  `ErrChannelClosed`; an out-of-range channel returns `ErrChecksum`.
- `(*Mux).CloseChannel(ch) error` closes one channel's write side: the
  FIN is itself a sequence entry (it takes one quota slot, so a full
  quota gives `ErrWindowFull` and the close is retried after acks); a
  channel that was never written is opened first, so an unused channel
  still delivers a clean EOF. Closing or writing an already closed
  channel returns `ErrChannelClosed`.
- `(*Mux).Flush() error` sends queued frames round-robin across
  channels (each pass serves at most one queued frame per channel,
  starting where the previous Flush stopped), so one busy channel can
  never starve another and a channel's frames never pass its own
  earlier frames. Every frame piggybacks the sender's current
  cumulative receive position for its channel; cumulative
  acknowledgements are also sent by a small background pump. As on the
  reliable layer, a writer that needs the peer's acks to drain quotas
  must let `ReadFrame` run.
- `(*Mux).ReadFrame() (ChannelFrame, error)` delivers across all
  channels: a gap-blocked channel never stalls another channel, while
  within a channel frames arrive in write order exactly once. After a
  channel's remaining frames, the read that reaches its FIN returns the
  `ChannelFrame` naming the channel together with `io.EOF`; other
  channels keep flowing. A channel number outside the session's reach,
  a residual older than one channel-window, a declaration more than one
  window ahead, an acknowledgement past the send frontier, a
  same-sequence retransmission with different content, an unknown flag,
  an ack carrying payload, or a damaged header is refused with
  `ErrChecksum`, stopping stickily at the current delivery positions.
  Reliable-layer results (`io.EOF`, `ErrShortFrame`, outer
  checksum/version/size and reader errors) pass through unchanged; when
  a terminal lower-layer read also brings complete frames, the buffered
  frames are delivered first.

Restart uses the same durable rules as the reliable layer: written data
frames are CRC-recorded in a shared journal (`mux.log`), acknowledged
per-channel positions in dual-slot checkpoints (`muxNNN.ckp`), and a
close marker (`muxNNN.closed`) survives a FIN whose journal prefix was
discarded. Recovery resumes each channel at the earlier of the
checkpoint and journal positions, so no unacknowledged frame is skipped
and the receiver deduplicates the overlap; a truncated journal or a
flipped bit in a complete record fails recovery with `ErrChecksum`. If
the close marker cannot be written, the close still takes effect: the
FIN is already journaled, so the in-memory state and the journal stay
consistent and a later restart recovers the same closed channel.

## Fragmentation and reassembly

`codec.NewFrag(m *Mux, cfg FragConfig) (*FragSession, error)` carries
whole payloads larger than the single-frame limit over one multiplexed
session: the caller writes each complete payload once and this layer
cuts it into ordered fragments that ride ordinary mux frames, so the
mux header, the reliable envelope, the codec frame, the header
constants and all established error values keep their exact semantics.
The fragment header lives only inside the mux payload
(`msg uint32`, `idx uint32`, `total uint32`, `flags uint8`,
`ack uint32`, `crc32`); no new error values are introduced.

- `FragConfig{MaxMessage int; StateDir string}`: the per-channel
  reassembly cap in bytes (no message may declare more) and a directory
  for the per-channel reassembly state files, created if missing.
- `FragFrame{Channel uint16; Flags uint16; Kind uint8; Payload []byte}`
  is the caller-visible message. `FragHeaderSize` (21) bytes are
  reserved inside the mux payload, so one fragment carries at most
  `FragMaxPayload = MuxMaxPayload - FragHeaderSize` chunk bytes.
- `(*FragSession).WriteFrame(FragFrame) error` slices the payload into
  ordered fragments and queues every fragment of the message
  atomically, so two messages of one channel never interleave; nothing
  goes out before `Flush`. A payload larger than `MaxMessage` returns
  `ErrTooLarge`; a channel whose in-flight quota is already exhausted
  returns `ErrWindowFull` (the same value as `ErrTooLarge`); both drop
  the write without consuming a message or frame sequence, so a
  rejected payload takes no buffer. Writing to a closed channel returns
  `ErrChannelClosed`; an out-of-range channel returns `ErrChecksum`.
- `(*FragSession).Flush() error` is the mux flush: fragments go out
  round-robin across channels, so one channel's fragments may be
  interleaved with other channels' frames, and a message whose
  fragments span several windows drains as acknowledgements arrive.
- `(*FragSession).ReadFrame() (FragFrame, error)` delivers one
  reassembled message per call, exactly once, with byte content and
  call order identical to the writes; a message stalled mid-assembly on
  one channel never blocks another channel's delivery. A fragment whose
  declared total exceeds the reassembly cap drops its whole message
  with `ErrTooLarge` and the stream continues. A fragment from an old
  message generation, one beyond the current receive position, a
  same-position duplicate with different content, an acknowledgement
  past the send frontier, an unknown flag, a malformed standalone
  acknowledgement, or a damaged fragment header is refused with
  `ErrChecksum` - the bare established value, comparable directly with
  `==` - and stops delivery stickily at the current position. Mux
  results (the per-channel `io.EOF` at a channel's FIN, the transport's
  `io.EOF`, `ErrShortFrame`, outer checksum/version/size and reader
  errors) pass through unchanged.
- `(*FragSession).CloseChannel(ch) error` closes the channel's write
  side through the mux and waits for the acknowledgement pump to wind
  down before returning; a second close returns `ErrChannelClosed`, and
  concurrent closes of one channel are safe.
- `(*FragSession).Close() error` stops the acknowledgement pump and
  closes the wrapped mux.

Restart uses the same durable rules as the lower layers: the send
position, the receive position and any partially reassembled message
are recorded per channel in a checksummed state file (`fragNNN.state`),
rewritten atomically on every accepted fragment, so an interrupted
reassembly resumes from the last confirmed position with no payload
delivered twice or skipped, and retransmitted fragments are
deduplicated. A state file that is truncated, torn or bit-flipped fails
recovery with `ErrChecksum`.

## Tests

    go test ./...

## Limits

Single frame in memory; no streaming reader in this scope.
No compression and no encryption.
Standard library only.

1	package codec
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/binary"
5		"io"
6		"sync"
7	)
8	
9	// flusher is implemented by buffered writers such as *bufio.Writer.
10	type flusher interface {
11		Flush() error
12	}
13	
14	// Session is a concurrency-safe multi-frame layer sitting on top of one
15	// byte writer and one byte reader. It does not change the wire format:
16	// every written frame is serialized with Encode and frames are simply
17	// concatenated, so the byte stream stays byte-for-byte compatible with
18	// the single-frame Encode/Decode entries.
19	//
20	// The two directions are independent and may be used concurrently:
21	//   - WriteFrame appends one whole encoded frame to an internal write
22	//     buffer; Flush writes everything buffered so far, in write order,
23	//     to the underlying writer.
24	//   - ReadFrame pulls bytes from the underlying reader in whatever
25	//     chunk sizes they arrive, keeps an incomplete trailing frame in an
26	//     internal buffer and returns one complete Frame per call.
27	//
28	// The total number of frames in a session is unbounded; the per-frame
29	// payload limit is MaxPayload, enforced at write time.
30	type Session struct {
31		w io.Writer
32		r io.Reader
33	
34		wmu  sync.Mutex
35		wbuf []byte
36	
37		rmu  sync.Mutex
38		rbuf []byte
39		// terminal error of the read side: a bad frame's error, io.EOF or
40		// an error reported by the underlying reader.
41		rerr error
42	}
43	
44	// NewSession returns a session writing to w and reading from r.
45	func NewSession(w io.Writer, r io.Reader) *Session {
46		return &Session{w: w, r: r}
47	}
48	
49	// WriteFrame encodes f with the single-frame encoder and appends the
50	// whole frame to the session's write buffer. Because Encode rejects an
51	// oversized payload before any byte is buffered, an ErrTooLarge result
52	// never leaves a partial frame behind, and concurrent writes never
53	// interleave the bytes of one frame with another. Writes become visible
54	// to the reader in call-arrival order once Flush runs.
55	func (s *Session) WriteFrame(f Frame) error {
56		b, err := Encode(f)
57		if err != nil {
58			return err
59		}
60		s.wmu.Lock()
61		s.wbuf = append(s.wbuf, b...)
62		s.wmu.Unlock()
63		return nil
64	}
65	
66	// Flush writes every buffered frame to the underlying writer as one
67	// ordered run and then, if the writer implements Flush itself (for
68	// example *bufio.Writer), flushes it. Bytes already appended by
69	// WriteFrame are never reordered or split across frames. If the
70	// underlying writer errors after a short write, the unsent tail is
71	// retained and a later Flush retries it.
72	func (s *Session) Flush() error {
73		s.wmu.Lock()
74		defer s.wmu.Unlock()
75	
76		pending := s.wbuf
77		for len(pending) > 0 {
78			n, err := s.w.Write(pending)
79			pending = pending[n:]
80			if err != nil {
81				// Keep the unsent tail at the front of the buffer so a
82				// later WriteFrame/Flush continues from exactly this point.
83				copy(s.wbuf, pending)
84				s.wbuf = s.wbuf[:len(pending)]
85				return err
86			}
87		}
88		s.wbuf = s.wbuf[:0]
89	
90		if f, ok := s.w.(flusher); ok {
91			return f.Flush()
92		}
93		return nil
94	}
95	
96	// ReadFrame returns the next complete frame, reading more bytes from the
97	// underlying reader only when the buffer cannot yet supply one. A
98	// truncated frame at the end of the input is buffered without error
99	// until more bytes arrive; it is reported as ErrShortFrame only when the
100	// reader signals end of input with bytes still outstanding. A clean end
101	// of input with no residual bytes returns io.EOF, i.e. reading simply
102	// stops.
103	//
104	// When a complete frame is corrupt, the error is the same value Decode
105	// would return for that frame (ErrBadVersion, ErrChecksum or
106	// ErrTooLarge); frame delivery stops there and the error becomes
107	// sticky, while every frame returned earlier already belongs to the
108	// caller. Concurrent ReadFrame calls are serialized, so each frame is
109	// delivered exactly once.
110	func (s *Session) ReadFrame() (Frame, error) {
111		s.rmu.Lock()
112		defer s.rmu.Unlock()
113	
114		if s.rerr != nil {
115			return Frame{}, s.rerr
116		}
117	
118		var scratch [4096]byte
119	
120		for {
121			// A frame can be handed to Decode only once its declared length
122			// is fully buffered; Decode then decides every error with exactly
123			// the same precedence the single-frame entry uses.
124			if len(s.rbuf) >= HeaderSize {
125				frameLen := uint64(HeaderSize) + uint64(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(s.rbuf[0:4]))
126				if uint64(len(s.rbuf)) >= frameLen {
127					f, err := Decode(s.rbuf[:int(frameLen)])
128					if err != nil {
129						return s.failRead(err)
130					}
131					// Drop the consumed frame and compact the residual bytes
132					// of later frames to the front; Decode copied the payload
133					// out, so overlapping storage is safe.
134					rest := len(s.rbuf) - int(frameLen)
135					copy(s.rbuf, s.rbuf[int(frameLen):])
136					s.rbuf = s.rbuf[:rest]
137					return f, nil
138				}
139			}
140	
141			n, err := s.r.Read(scratch[:])
142			if n > 0 {
143				s.rbuf = append(s.rbuf, scratch[:n]...)
144			}
145			if err == nil {
146				// A (0, nil) read delivers no information; retry instead of
147				// mistaking it for end of input.
148				continue
149			}
150			if err == io.EOF {
151				if len(s.rbuf) > 0 {
152					return s.failRead(ErrShortFrame)
153				}
154				return s.failRead(io.EOF)
155			}
156			return s.failRead(err)
157		}
158	}
159	
160	// failRead records the terminal read-side error and returns it with the
161	// zero frame.
162	func (s *Session) failRead(err error) (Frame, error) {
163		s.rerr = err
164		return Frame{}, err
165	}
166

1	package codec

4		"bytes"
5		"encoding/binary"
6		"errors"
7		"fmt"
8		"hash/crc32"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sync"

14	
15	// Fragmentation and reassembly on top of one Mux.
16	//
17	// A FragSession lets the caller write one complete payload per call even
18	// when it exceeds the single-frame limit: the send side cuts the payload
19	// into ordered fragments and every fragment rides an ordinary mux frame,
20	// so the mux layer, the reliable layer, the codec frame format and every
21	// established entry, constant and error value below this layer keep
22	// their exact semantics. The fragment header lives only inside the mux
23	// payload.
24	//
25	// Fragment header layout inside a mux payload (all multi-byte fields
26	// big-endian):
27	//
28	//		+---------+---------+-----------+--------+---------+----------+=========+
29	//		| msg (4) | idx (4) | total (4) | fl (1) | ack (4) | crc32(4) | chunk   |
30	//		+---------+---------+-----------+--------+---------+----------+=========+
31	//
32	//	  - msg: per-channel message sequence, numbered in write order; every
33	//	    fragment of one message carries the same msg.
34	//	  - idx: fragment index within the message, 0-based; every chunk
35	//	    except the last carries exactly FragMaxPayload bytes.
36	//	  - total: total payload bytes of the whole message.
37	//	  - fl: 1 = LAST, the message's final fragment; 2 = standalone
38	//	    cumulative acknowledgement (msg/idx/total are zero, no chunk).
39	//	    The two are never combined.
40	//	  - ack: cumulative "next expected message" for the channel,
41	//	    piggybacked on every fragment: every message of the channel with
42	//	    msg < ack has been delivered to the reader.
43	//	  - crc32: IEEE CRC of the other 17 header bytes plus the chunk.
44	//
45	// The mux payload limit stays MuxMaxPayload; FragHeaderSize bytes are
46	// reserved, so one fragment carries at most FragMaxPayload chunk bytes.
47	//
48	// Delivery guarantees:
49	//   - Messages within one channel are delivered in write order exactly
50	//     once, with byte content identical to what was written; fragments of
51	//     one message never interleave with another message of the same
52	//     channel. Channels are independent: a message stalled mid-assembly
53	//     on one channel never blocks another channel's delivery.
54	//   - The send side numbers messages in write order and queues every
55	//     fragment of an accepted message atomically; nothing goes out
56	//     before Flush. A payload larger than the configured per-channel
57	//     reassembly cap returns ErrTooLarge, and a channel whose in-flight
58	//     quota is already exhausted returns ErrWindowFull (the same value
59	//     as ErrTooLarge); both drop the write without consuming a message
60	//     or frame sequence, so a rejected payload takes no buffer.
61	//   - The receive side keeps one bounded reassembly buffer per channel
62	//     (at most MaxMessage bytes). A fragment whose declared total
63	//     exceeds the cap is dropped with ErrTooLarge and the stream
64	//     continues. A fragment from an old message generation, one beyond
65	//     the current receive position, a same-position duplicate with
66	//     different content, an acknowledgement past the send frontier, or
67	//     a damaged fragment header is refused with ErrChecksum - the bare
68	//     established value, comparable with == - and stops delivery
69	//     stickily at the current position.
70	//
71	// As on the lower layers, nothing is transmitted before Flush; after a
72	// restart the mux journal resends every unconfirmed fragment, so Flush
73	// is also the retransmit operation and the receiver deduplicates the
74	// overlap.
75	const (
76		// FragHeaderSize is this layer's per-fragment overhead:
77		// 4 (msg) + 4 (idx) + 4 (total) + 1 (flags) + 4 (ack) + 4 (crc32).
78		FragHeaderSize = 4 + 4 + 4 + 1 + 4 + 4
79	
80		// FragMaxPayload is the largest chunk one fragment may carry;
81		// FragHeaderSize bytes are reserved inside the mux payload, whose
82		// own limit stays MuxMaxPayload.
83		FragMaxPayload = MuxMaxPayload - FragHeaderSize
84	
85		// fragment header field offsets.
86		fhMsgOff   = 0
87		fhIdxOff   = 4
88		fhTotalOff = 8
89		fhFlagOff  = 12
90		fhAckOff   = 13
91		fhCRCOff   = 17
92		fhBodyOff  = 21
93	
94		fhFlagLast = 1 << 0
95		fhFlagAck  = 1 << 1
96	)
97	
98	// FragConfig configures a FragSession.
99	type FragConfig struct {
100		// MaxMessage is the per-channel reassembly cap in bytes: the largest
101		// total payload one message may declare. It must be positive and fit
102		// a uint32. Both peers of one connection should use the same cap.
103		MaxMessage int
104	
105		// StateDir holds the per-channel reassembly state files used to
106		// resume message numbering and interrupted reassemblies after a
107		// restart. It is created if missing.
108		StateDir string
109	}
110	
111	// FragFrame is one caller-visible message on the fragmentation layer.
112	// Channel names the channel it was written to.
113	type FragFrame struct {
114		Channel uint16
115		Flags   uint16
116		Kind    uint8
117		Payload []byte
118	}
119	
120	// fragRecv is one channel's receive-side reassembly state. While a
121	// message is being assembled, buf holds the chunks received so far;
122	// every chunk in an incomplete message is exactly FragMaxPayload bytes,
123	// so a retransmitted chunk is compared against buf at idx*FragMaxPayload.
124	type fragRecv struct {
125		next     uint32 // next message sequence due for delivery
126		started  bool   // a message is mid-assembly
127		dropping bool   // an over-cap message is being skipped until its LAST
128		ptotal   uint32
129		pflags   uint16
130		pkind    uint8
131		buf      []byte
132	}
133	
134	// FragSession is a fragmentation layer wrapping one Mux. Create it with
135	// NewFrag; the wrapped mux must not be used directly while the
136	// FragSession owns it.
137	type FragSession struct {
138		mux      *Mux
139		cfg      FragConfig
140		channels int
141	
142		// mu guards every piece of mutable state below; WriteFrame holds it
143		// across the mux batch so two concurrent writes can never interleave
144		// the fragments of two messages on one channel. ReadFrame never
145		// holds it while blocked in the mux reader.
146		mu       sync.Mutex
147		sendNext []uint32
148		recv     []fragRecv
149		rerr     error
150	
151		// ackPoke coalescingly wakes the acknowledgement pump (capacity 1 is
152		// enough because acks are cumulative and the pump reads the latest
153		// positions under mu); syncCh carries rendezvous requests from
154		// CloseChannel, which returns only after the pump has wound down.
155		ackPoke   chan struct{}
156		syncCh    chan chan struct{}
157		stopCh    chan struct{}
158		doneCh    chan struct{}
159		closeOnce sync.Once
160	}
161	
162	// NewFrag wraps m in a fragmentation session. Reassembly state in
163	// cfg.StateDir is consulted when present: a fresh directory starts every
164	// channel at message 0, while a directory left by a crashed or restarted
165	// process resumes message numbering and any interrupted reassembly from
166	// the last confirmed positions. A state file that is truncated, torn or
167	// bit-flipped fails recovery with ErrChecksum rather than reassembling
168	// unverified bytes.
169	func NewFrag(m *Mux, cfg FragConfig) (*FragSession, error) {
170		if cfg.MaxMessage <= 0 || cfg.MaxMessage > 1<<32-1 {
171			return nil, errors.New("codec: frag max message size must be in (0, 2^32)")
172		}
173		if cfg.StateDir == "" {
174			return nil, errors.New("codec: frag session requires a state directory")
175		}
176		if err := os.MkdirAll(cfg.StateDir, 0o755); err != nil {
177			return nil, err
178		}
179	
180		nch := m.cfg.Channels
181		fs := &FragSession{
182			mux:      m,
183			cfg:      cfg,
184			channels: nch,
185			sendNext: make([]uint32, nch),
186			recv:     make([]fragRecv, nch),
187			ackPoke:  make(chan struct{}, 1),
188			syncCh:   make(chan chan struct{}),
189			stopCh:   make(chan struct{}),
190			doneCh:   make(chan struct{}),
191		}
192		for ch := 0; ch < nch; ch++ {
193			sendNext, rc, err := loadFragState(cfg.StateDir, uint16(ch), cfg.MaxMessage)
194			if err != nil {
195				return nil, err
196			}
197			fs.sendNext[ch] = sendNext
198			fs.recv[ch] = rc
199		}
200	
201		// The mux journal may hold fragments newer than the last persisted
202		// send position (a crash between journaling and the state write):
203		// resume numbering past anything already journaled so a rewritten
204		// message can never collide with one the peer may have received.
205		for _, rec := range m.log.recs {
206			if int(rec.ch) >= nch {
207				continue
208			}
209			msg, _, _, flags, _, _, err := decodeFragHeader(rec.f.Payload)
210			if err != nil || flags&fhFlagAck != 0 {
211				continue
212			}
213			if msg+1 > fs.sendNext[rec.ch] {
214				fs.sendNext[rec.ch] = msg + 1
215			}
216		}
217	
218		go fs.pumpAck()
219		return fs, nil
220	}
221	
222	// WriteFrame slices f.Payload into ordered fragments and queues every
223	// fragment on channel f.Channel as ordinary mux frames; nothing reaches
224	// the wire before Flush. The whole message is accepted atomically, so
225	// its fragments can never interleave with another message of the same
226	// channel.
227	//
228	// It returns ErrTooLarge for a payload larger than the configured
229	// reassembly cap, ErrChecksum for a channel number outside the session,
230	// ErrWindowFull (the same value as ErrTooLarge) when the channel's
231	// in-flight quota is already exhausted, and ErrChannelClosed when the
232	// channel's write side has been closed. A rejected payload is neither
233	// queued nor journaled and consumes no message or frame sequence.
234	func (fs *FragSession) WriteFrame(f FragFrame) error {
235		if len(f.Payload) > fs.cfg.MaxMessage {
236			return ErrTooLarge
237		}
238		if int(f.Channel) >= fs.channels {
239			return ErrChecksum
240		}
241	
242		fs.mu.Lock()
243		defer fs.mu.Unlock()
244	
245		msg := fs.sendNext[f.Channel]
246		total := uint32(len(f.Payload))
247		n := 1
248		if len(f.Payload) > 0 {
249			n = (len(f.Payload) + FragMaxPayload - 1) / FragMaxPayload
250		}
251		frames := make([]ChannelFrame, 0, n)
252		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
253			lo := i * FragMaxPayload
254			hi := lo + FragMaxPayload
255			if hi > len(f.Payload) {
256				hi = len(f.Payload)
257			}
258			flags := uint8(0)
259			if i == n-1 {
260				flags = fhFlagLast
261			}
262			frames = append(frames, ChannelFrame{
263				Channel: f.Channel,
264				Flags:   f.Flags,
265				Kind:    f.Kind,
266				Payload: encodeFragHeader(msg, uint32(i), total, flags,
267					fs.recv[f.Channel].next, f.Payload[lo:hi]),
268			})
269		}
270		if err := fs.mux.writeFragments(frames); err != nil {
271			return err
272		}
273		fs.sendNext[f.Channel]++
274		// The send position is durable before the write returns: after a
275		// restart, numbering must never reuse a message sequence the peer
276		// may already have received.
277		return fs.persistLocked(f.Channel)
278	}
279	
280	// Flush sends every queued fragment through the wrapped mux: fragments
281	// go out round-robin across channels, so one channel's fragments may be
282	// interleaved with other channels' frames but never overtake an earlier
283	// fragment of their own channel. After a restart the queue was reloaded
284	// from the journal, so Flush is also the retransmit operation.
285	func (fs *FragSession) Flush() error {
286		return fs.mux.Flush()
287	}
288	
289	// ReadFrame returns the next completely reassembled message across all
290	// channels, exactly once. Fragments of one channel arrive in write
291	// order; a channel whose current message is still incomplete never
292	// blocks another channel's delivery.
293	//
294	// A fragment declaring a total larger than the reassembly cap drops its
295	// whole message with ErrTooLarge and the stream continues. The
296	// following are refused with the bare established ErrChecksum value and
297	// stop delivery stickily at the current position: a fragment from an
298	// old message generation, one beyond the current receive position, a
299	// same-position duplicate with different content, an acknowledgement
300	// past the send frontier, an unknown flag, a malformed standalone
301	// acknowledgement, and a damaged fragment header. Mux results (the
302	// per-channel io.EOF at a channel's FIN, the transport's io.EOF,
303	// ErrShortFrame, outer checksum/version/size and reader errors) pass
304	// through unchanged.
305	func (fs *FragSession) ReadFrame() (FragFrame, error) {
306		for {
307			fs.mu.Lock()
308			if fs.rerr != nil {
309				err := fs.rerr
310				fs.mu.Unlock()
311				return FragFrame{}, err
312			}
313			// A message whose final fragment already arrived is finalized
314			// (position persisted) and delivered here, so a persist failure
315			// is retried on the next call instead of losing the message.
316			if ff, ok, err := fs.tryFinalizeLocked(); err != nil {
317				fs.mu.Unlock()
318				return FragFrame{}, err
319			} else if ok {
320				fs.mu.Unlock()
321				return ff, nil
322			}
323			fs.mu.Unlock()
324	
325			// Block in the mux reader WITHOUT holding mu, exactly like the
326			// lower layers: sends and ack processing must keep moving while
327			// this waits for bytes.
328			cf, rerr := fs.mux.ReadFrame()
329			if rerr != nil {
330				if errors.Is(rerr, io.EOF) {
331					// A channel's FIN (or the transport end) passes through
332					// with the channel named, as the mux reported it.
333					return FragFrame{Channel: cf.Channel}, io.EOF
334				}
335				return FragFrame{}, rerr
336			}
337	
338			msg, idx, total, flags, ack, chunk, err := decodeFragHeader(cf.Payload)
339			if err != nil {
340				return fs.failRead(ErrChecksum)
341			}
342			ch := cf.Channel
343	
344			fs.mu.Lock()
345			if fs.rerr != nil {
346				err := fs.rerr
347				fs.mu.Unlock()
348				return FragFrame{}, err
349			}
350	
351			// Every inbound message states a cumulative position for its
352			// channel; one past anything this side ever sent is impossible
353			// in a well-behaved stream and is refused before anything else.
354			if ack > fs.sendNext[ch] {
355				return fs.failReadLocked(ErrChecksum)
356			}
357	
358			if flags&fhFlagAck != 0 {
359				// A standalone acknowledgement carries no fragment.
360				if flags != fhFlagAck || msg != 0 || idx != 0 || total != 0 || len(chunk) != 0 {
361					return fs.failReadLocked(ErrChecksum)
362				}
363				fs.mu.Unlock()
364				continue
365			}
366			if flags&^uint8(fhFlagLast) != 0 {
367				return fs.failReadLocked(ErrChecksum)
368			}
369			last := flags&fhFlagLast != 0
370	
371			rc := &fs.recv[ch]
372			// Only the message currently due may arrive: anything older is
373			// an old-generation residual, anything newer is beyond the
374			// receive position's reach.
375			if msg != rc.next {
376				return fs.failReadLocked(ErrChecksum)
377			}
378	
379			if rc.dropping {
380				// Skip the remaining fragments of a dropped over-cap
381				// message; its LAST fragment retires it.
382				if last {
383					rc.dropping = false
384					rc.next++
385					fs.signalAckLocked()
386				}
387				fs.mu.Unlock()
388				continue
389			}
390	
391			if !rc.started {
392				if idx != 0 {
393					// A message starting past its first fragment is
394					// unreachable from the current position.
395					return fs.failReadLocked(ErrChecksum)
396				}
397				if uint64(total) > uint64(fs.cfg.MaxMessage) {
398					// The declared total exceeds the reassembly cap: drop
399					// the whole message with the established over-limit
400					// value; the stream itself continues.
401					rc.dropping = true
402					rc.ptotal = total
403					if last {
404						rc.dropping = false
405						rc.next++
406					}
407					fs.signalAckLocked()
408					fs.mu.Unlock()
409					return FragFrame{}, ErrTooLarge
410				}
411				if err := checkFragChunk(total, idx, last, chunk); err != nil {
412					return fs.failReadLocked(ErrChecksum)
413				}
414				rc.started = true
415				rc.ptotal = total
416				rc.pflags = cf.Flags
417				rc.pkind = cf.Kind
418				rc.buf = append(rc.buf[:0], chunk...)
419			} else {
420				if total != rc.ptotal {
421					return fs.failReadLocked(ErrChecksum)
422				}
423				// Every chunk of an incomplete message is full-size, so the
424				// next index due is exact.
425				nextIdx := uint32(len(rc.buf) / FragMaxPayload)
426				switch {
427				case idx < nextIdx:
428					// A retransmission of a stored fragment must describe
429					// the same fragment; a conflicting duplicate is refused
430					// instead of guessed.
431					off := int(idx) * FragMaxPayload
432					if last || !bytes.Equal(rc.buf[off:off+FragMaxPayload], chunk) {
433						return fs.failReadLocked(ErrChecksum)
434					}
435					fs.mu.Unlock()
436					continue
437				case idx > nextIdx:
438					return fs.failReadLocked(ErrChecksum)
439				}
440				if err := checkFragChunk(total, idx, last, chunk); err != nil {
441					return fs.failReadLocked(ErrChecksum)
442				}
443				rc.buf = append(rc.buf, chunk...)
444			}
445			// Write the reassembly state through before the mux can
446			// acknowledge this fragment past the sender: after a restart the
447			// assembly resumes from exactly this position.
448			_ = fs.persistLocked(ch)
449			fs.signalAckLocked()
450			fs.mu.Unlock()
451		}
452	}
453	
454	// tryFinalizeLocked delivers one channel's just-completed message. The
455	// advanced receive position is persisted BEFORE the message is handed
456	// out, so a restart never delivers it twice; on a persist failure the
457	// state is rolled back and retried on a later call. Caller holds mu.
458	func (fs *FragSession) tryFinalizeLocked() (FragFrame, bool, error) {
459		for ch := 0; ch < fs.channels; ch++ {
460			rc := &fs.recv[ch]
461			if !rc.started || rc.dropping || uint64(len(rc.buf)) != uint64(rc.ptotal) {
462				continue
463			}
464			ff := FragFrame{Channel: uint16(ch), Flags: rc.pflags, Kind: rc.pkind, Payload: rc.buf}
465			rc.next++
466			rc.started = false
467			rc.buf = nil
468			if err := fs.persistLocked(uint16(ch)); err != nil {
469				rc.next--
470				rc.started = true
471				rc.buf = ff.Payload
472				return FragFrame{}, false, err
473			}
474			fs.signalAckLocked()
475			return ff, true, nil
476		}
477		return FragFrame{}, false, nil
478	}
479	
480	// failRead records the terminal read-side result and returns it.
481	func (fs *FragSession) failRead(err error) (FragFrame, error) {
482		fs.mu.Lock()
483		fs.rerr = err
484		fs.mu.Unlock()
485		return FragFrame{}, err
486	}
487	
488	// failReadLocked is failRead with mu already held; it releases mu.
489	func (fs *FragSession) failReadLocked(err error) (FragFrame, error) {
490		fs.rerr = err
491		fs.mu.Unlock()
492		return FragFrame{}, err
493	}
494	
495	// signalAckLocked coalescingly asks the acknowledgement pump to restate
496	// the receive positions. It never blocks. Caller holds mu.
497	func (fs *FragSession) signalAckLocked() {
498		select {
499		case fs.ackPoke <- struct{}{}:
500		default:
501		}
502	}
503	
504	// pumpAck serializes standalone acknowledgement writes so they happen on
505	// this goroutine, never on a reader's. Every wakeup sends at most one
506	// cumulative ack per channel whose receive position moved since the last
507	// send, so a burst of fragments costs a handful of frames rather than
508	// one per arrival.
509	func (fs *FragSession) pumpAck() {
510		defer close(fs.doneCh)
511		sent := make([]uint32, fs.channels)
512		for {
513			select {
514			case <-fs.stopCh:
515				return
516			case <-fs.ackPoke:
517				fs.sendAcks(sent)
518			case done := <-fs.syncCh:
519				fs.sendAcks(sent)
520				close(done)
521			}
522		}
523	}
524	
525	// sendAcks writes one standalone cumulative acknowledgement for every
526	// channel whose receive position moved since sent. Best effort: a
527	// failed or blocked ack is harmless because every later fragment
528	// piggybacks the same cumulative position.
529	func (fs *FragSession) sendAcks(sent []uint32) {
530		fs.mu.Lock()
531		pos := make([]uint32, fs.channels)
532		for ch := range pos {
533			pos[ch] = fs.recv[ch].next
534		}
535		fs.mu.Unlock()
536	
537		wrote := false
538		for ch := 0; ch < fs.channels; ch++ {
539			if pos[ch] == sent[ch] {
540				continue
541			}
542			hdr := encodeFragHeader(0, 0, 0, fhFlagAck, pos[ch], nil)
543			if err := fs.mux.WriteFrame(ChannelFrame{Channel: uint16(ch), Payload: hdr}); err != nil {
544				continue
545			}
546			sent[ch] = pos[ch]
547			wrote = true
548		}
549		if wrote {
550			_ = fs.mux.Flush()
551		}
552	}
553	
554	// CloseChannel closes the write side of ch through the wrapped mux and
555	// waits for the acknowledgement pump to wind down before returning, so
556	// every position delivered before the close is on its way to the peer.
557	// Closing (or writing to) an already closed channel returns
558	// ErrChannelClosed; an out-of-range channel returns ErrChecksum. Both
559	// values compare equal to the established sentinels directly.
560	func (fs *FragSession) CloseChannel(ch uint16) error {
561		if int(ch) >= fs.channels {
562			return ErrChecksum
563		}
564		if err := fs.mux.CloseChannel(ch); err != nil {
565			return err
566		}
567		// Rendezvous with the pump: it answers after flushing every
568		// acknowledgement queued so far. If it already stopped (Close), or
569		// stops before answering, the rendezvous completes immediately.
570		done := make(chan struct{})
571		select {
572		case fs.syncCh <- done:
573			select {
574			case <-done:
575			case <-fs.doneCh:
576			}
577		case <-fs.doneCh:
578		}
579		return nil
580	}
581	
582	// Close stops the acknowledgement pump, waits for it to wind down and
583	// closes the wrapped mux. Fully journaled but unacknowledged fragments
584	// remain in the mux journal for a later restart to resend.
585	func (fs *FragSession) Close() error {
586		fs.closeOnce.Do(func() { close(fs.stopCh) })
587		<-fs.doneCh
588		return fs.mux.Close()
589	}
590	
591	// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
592	// Fragment header encoding.
593	// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
594	
595	// encodeFragHeader serializes one fragment header plus its chunk into
596	// mux payload bytes.
597	func encodeFragHeader(msg, idx, total uint32, flags uint8, ack uint32, chunk []byte) []byte {
598		out := make([]byte, FragHeaderSize+len(chunk))
599		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[fhMsgOff:fhIdxOff], msg)
600		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[fhIdxOff:fhTotalOff], idx)
601		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[fhTotalOff:fhFlagOff], total)
602		out[fhFlagOff] = flags
603		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[fhAckOff:fhCRCOff], ack)
604		copy(out[fhBodyOff:], chunk)
605		h := crc32.NewIEEE()
606		h.Write(out[:fhCRCOff])
607		h.Write(out[fhBodyOff:])
608		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[fhCRCOff:fhBodyOff], h.Sum32())
609		return out
610	}
611	
612	// decodeFragHeader parses one fragment header. A message too short for
613	// the fixed header or one whose CRC does not match is reported with the
614	// established checksum value.
615	func decodeFragHeader(p []byte) (msg, idx, total uint32, flags uint8, ack uint32, chunk []byte, err error) {
616		if len(p) < FragHeaderSize {
617			return 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, nil, ErrChecksum
618		}
619		h := crc32.NewIEEE()
620		h.Write(p[:fhCRCOff])
621		h.Write(p[fhBodyOff:])
622		if h.Sum32() != binary.BigEndian.Uint32(p[fhCRCOff:fhBodyOff]) {
623			return 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, nil, ErrChecksum
624		}
625		msg = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(p[fhMsgOff:fhIdxOff])
626		idx = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(p[fhIdxOff:fhTotalOff])
627		total = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(p[fhTotalOff:fhFlagOff])
628		flags = p[fhFlagOff]
629		ack = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(p[fhAckOff:fhCRCOff])
630		body := make([]byte, len(p)-FragHeaderSize)
631		copy(body, p[fhBodyOff:])
632		return msg, idx, total, flags, ack, body, nil
633	}
634	
635	// fragCount is the number of fragments a message of total bytes splits
636	// into; an empty message is exactly one (empty) fragment.
637	func fragCount(total uint32) uint32 {
638		if total == 0 {
639			return 1
640		}
641		return uint32((uint64(total) + FragMaxPayload - 1) / FragMaxPayload)
642	}
643	
644	// checkFragChunk validates one fragment's shape against the message's
645	// declared total: the index must belong to the message, the LAST
646	// marking must fall exactly on the final index, and the chunk must
647	// carry exactly its share of the declared bytes.
648	func checkFragChunk(total, idx uint32, last bool, chunk []byte) error {
649		fc := fragCount(total)
650		if idx >= fc {
651			return ErrChecksum
652		}
653		if last != (idx == fc-1) {
654			return ErrChecksum
655		}
656		want := FragMaxPayload
657		if idx == fc-1 {
658			want = int(total) - int(idx)*FragMaxPayload
659		}
660		if len(chunk) != want {
661			return ErrChecksum
662		}
663		return nil
664	}
665	
666	// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
667	// Durable state: one checksummed reassembly state file per channel,
668	// rewritten atomically via temp file + rename on every accepted
669	// fragment, so an interrupted reassembly resumes from the last confirmed
670	// position and a delivered message is never delivered twice.
671	//
672	// File layout (all multi-byte fields big-endian):
673	//
674	//	+------------+------------+----------+-----------------------+----------+
675	//	| send (4)   | recv (4)   | mode (1) | [partial record]      | crc32(4) |
676	//	+------------+------------+----------+-----------------------+----------+
677	//
678	// mode 0 carries no partial record. mode 1 (assembly in progress)
679	// carries: total(4) flags(2) kind(1) datalen(4) data(datalen).
680	// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
681	
682	const (
683		fragStatePrefix = "frag"
684		fragStateSuffix = ".state"
685	
686		fragStateHdrSize = 4 + 4 + 1 // sendNext + recvNext + mode
687	
688		fragModeNone    = 0
689		fragModePartial = 1
690	)
691	
692	// fragDiskState is one channel's persisted state.
693	type fragDiskState struct {
694		sendNext uint32
695		recvNext uint32
696		mode     uint8
697		ptotal   uint32
698		pflags   uint16
699		pkind    uint8
700		pdata    []byte
701	}
702	
703	func fragStatePath(dir string, ch uint16) string {
704		return filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("%s%03d%s", fragStatePrefix, ch, fragStateSuffix))
705	}
706	
707	// persistLocked writes the channel's current state through to its state
708	// file. Caller holds mu.
709	func (fs *FragSession) persistLocked(ch uint16) error {
710		rc := &fs.recv[ch]
711		st := fragDiskState{
712			sendNext: fs.sendNext[ch],
713			recvNext: rc.next,
714		}
715		if rc.started && !rc.dropping {
716			st.mode = fragModePartial
717			st.ptotal = rc.ptotal
718			st.pflags = rc.pflags
719			st.pkind = rc.pkind
720			st.pdata = rc.buf
721		}
722		return saveFragState(fs.cfg.StateDir, ch, st)
723	}
724	
725	func marshalFragState(st fragDiskState) []byte {
726		body := make([]byte, 0, fragStateHdrSize+11+len(st.pdata)+4)
727		var tmp [4]byte
728		put32 := func(v uint32) {
729			binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(tmp[:], v)
730			body = append(body, tmp[:]...)
731		}
732		put32(st.sendNext)
733		put32(st.recvNext)
734		body = append(body, st.mode)
735		if st.mode == fragModePartial {
736			put32(st.ptotal)
737			binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(tmp[:2], st.pflags)
738			body = append(body, tmp[:2]...)
739			body = append(body, st.pkind)
740			put32(uint32(len(st.pdata)))
741			body = append(body, st.pdata...)
742		}
743		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(tmp[:], crc32.ChecksumIEEE(body))
744		return append(body, tmp[:]...)
745	}

747	// saveFragState rewrites the channel's state file atomically.
748	func saveFragState(dir string, ch uint16, st fragDiskState) error {
749		path := fragStatePath(dir, ch)
750		tmp := path + ".tmp"
751		f, err := os.OpenFile(tmp, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_TRUNC, 0o644)
752		if err != nil {
753			return err
754		}
755		if _, err := f.Write(marshalFragState(st)); err != nil {
756			f.Close()
757			return err
758		}
759		if err := f.Sync(); err != nil {
760			f.Close()
761			return err
762		}
763		if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
764			return err
765		}
766		return os.Rename(tmp, path)
767	}
768	
769	// loadFragState reads one channel's state file strictly: every byte must
770	// belong to one complete, valid record. A missing file means a fresh
771	// channel; a truncated file, a bad CRC, an unknown mode or an
772	// inconsistent partial record fails recovery with ErrChecksum rather
773	// than reassembling unverified bytes.
774	func loadFragState(dir string, ch uint16, maxMessage int) (sendNext uint32, rc fragRecv, err error) {
775		data, err := os.ReadFile(fragStatePath(dir, ch))
776		if err != nil {
777			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
778				return 0, fragRecv{}, nil
779			}
780			return 0, fragRecv{}, err
781		}
782		fail := func() (uint32, fragRecv, error) {
783			return 0, fragRecv{}, fmt.Errorf("codec: frag state %s corrupted: %w",
784				filepath.Base(fragStatePath(dir, ch)), ErrChecksum)
785		}
786		if len(data) < fragStateHdrSize+4 {
787			return fail()
788		}
789		body := data[:len(data)-4]
790		if crc32.ChecksumIEEE(body) != binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[len(data)-4:]) {
791			return fail()
792		}
793		sendNext = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(body[0:4])
794		rc.next = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(body[4:8])
795		mode := body[8]
796		switch mode {
797		case fragModeNone:
798			if len(body) != fragStateHdrSize {
799				return fail()
800			}
801		case fragModePartial:
802			if len(body) < fragStateHdrSize+11 {
803				return fail()
804			}
805			ptotal := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(body[9:13])
806			pflags := binary.BigEndian.Uint16(body[13:15])
807			pkind := body[15]
808			dlen := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(body[16:20])
809			if len(body) != fragStateHdrSize+11+int(dlen) {
810				return fail()
811			}
812			// A partial assembly holds only whole full-size chunks, plus
813			// possibly the final short chunk of a message that completed
814			// exactly as the process stopped (an empty message stops with
815			// zero bytes); anything else cannot have been written by this
816			// layer.
817			if uint64(ptotal) > uint64(maxMessage) || dlen > ptotal ||
818				(dlen < ptotal && (dlen == 0 || dlen%FragMaxPayload != 0)) {
819				return fail()
820			}
821			rc.started = true
822			rc.ptotal = ptotal
823			rc.pflags = pflags
824			rc.pkind = pkind
825			rc.buf = append([]byte(nil), body[fragStateHdrSize+11:]...)
826		default:
827			return fail()
828		}
829		return sendNext, rc, nil
830	}

15	// Channel multiplexing on top of one ReliableSession.
16	//
17	// A Mux carries several independent logical channels over a single
18	// reliable session. Every multiplexed message is the payload of one
19	// reliable data frame, prefixed by this layer's own mux header; the
20	// reliable wire format, the codec frame format and every established
21	// entry, constant and error value below this layer keep their exact
22	// byte-level semantics.
23	//
24	// Mux header layout inside a reliable payload (all multi-byte fields
25	// big-endian):
26	//
27	//		+----------+---------+--------+---------+----------+=========+
28	//		| chan (2) | seq (4) | fl (1) | ack (4) | crc32(4) | payload |
29	//		+----------+---------+--------+---------+----------+=========+
30	//
31	//	  - chan: the channel number the frame belongs to.
32	//	  - seq: per-channel write sequence, numbered in write order; an ack
33	//	    frame carries no data seq and sets it to zero.
34	//	  - fl: 1 = FIN, the channel's closing frame (no payload, no caller
35	//	    flags/kind); 2 = standalone cumulative acknowledgement. The two
36	//	    are never combined.
37	//	  - ack: cumulative "next expected" acknowledgement for chan,
38	//	    piggybacked on every message: every data frame of chan with seq
39	//	    < ack has been delivered to the reader.
40	//	  - crc32: IEEE CRC of the other 11 header bytes plus the payload.
41	//
42	// The reliable frame's own payload limit stays ReliableMaxPayload;
43	// MuxHeaderSize bytes are reserved, so the inner payload limit is
44	// MuxMaxPayload.
45	//
46	// Delivery guarantees:
47	//   - Frames within one channel are delivered in write order exactly
48	//     once; channels are independent, so a gap on one channel never
49	//     blocks another channel's delivery.
50	//   - The send side hands transmission opportunities out round-robin
51	//     across channels, so one channel sending continuously can never
52	//     starve the others.
53	//   - Every channel has its own in-flight quota; a write that finds the
54	//     quota full returns the established over-limit value ErrWindowFull
55	//     and an oversized payload returns ErrTooLarge. A rejected frame is
56	//     neither queued nor journaled and consumes no sequence, so it takes
57	//     no quota; the total buffer is bounded by Channels*Window frames.
58	//   - A channel opens on its first write and its write side can be
59	//     closed independently; its FIN rides the sequence stream like a
60	//     data frame. After the peer has received the channel's remaining
61	//     frames, the read that reaches the FIN returns io.EOF together with
62	//     a ChannelFrame naming the channel; other channels keep flowing.
63	//     Writing to, or closing, an already closed channel returns
64	//     ErrChannelClosed.
65	//
66	// As on the reliable layer, nothing is transmitted before Flush; after
67	// a restart the queue is reloaded from the journal, so Flush is also the
68	// retransmit operation.
69	const (
70		// MuxHeaderSize is this layer's per-frame overhead:
71		// 2 (chan) + 4 (seq) + 1 (flags) + 4 (ack) + 4 (crc32).
72		MuxHeaderSize = 2 + 4 + 1 + 4 + 4
73	
74		// MuxMaxPayload is the largest payload a multiplexed data frame may
75		// carry; MuxHeaderSize bytes are reserved inside the reliable
76		// payload, whose own limit stays ReliableMaxPayload.
77		MuxMaxPayload = ReliableMaxPayload - MuxHeaderSize

81		mhSeqOff  = 2
82		mhFlagOff = 6
83		mhAckOff  = 7
84		mhCRCOff  = 11
85		mhBodyOff = 15

87		mhFlagFin = 1 << 0
88		mhFlagAck = 1 << 1

92	// write side has already been closed.

95	// MuxConfig configures a Mux.
96	type MuxConfig struct {
97		// Channels is the number of logical channels the session carries,
98		// numbered 0..Channels-1. It must be positive.
99		Channels int
100	
101		// Window is the per-channel in-flight quota in frames, enforced
102		// independently for every channel (and the receive-side reach used
103		// to place inbound sequences). It must be positive.
104		Window int

106		// StateDir holds the per-channel checkpoint files and the shared
107		// replay journal used to resume the write side after a restart. It

113	// the channel it was written to.

116		Flags   uint16
117		Kind    uint8
118		Payload []byte
119	}

122	// transmission opportunity or an acknowledgement.
123	type queuedFrame struct {

125		seq     uint32
126		flags   uint16

135		// "next expected" position confirmed by the peer. In-flight quota is

137		next   uint32

141	}

148	}

154	}

156	// Mux is a multiplexing layer wrapping one ReliableSession. Create it
157	// with NewMux; the wrapped session must not be used directly while the
158	// Mux owns it.

160		rel *ReliableSession
161		cfg MuxConfig
162	
163		mu    sync.Mutex
164		queue []*queuedFrame // accepted, unacknowledged frames, arrival order
165		sc    []sendChannel
166		// rr is the round-robin cursor: the channel at which the next Flush
167		// starts handing out opportunities.
168		rr  int
169		log *muxLog
170	
171		rmu sync.Mutex

173		// channels whose FIN already reached the reader. seen remembers the
174		// first copy of every sequence inside the duplicate span (the
175		// window width behind the base) so a retransmitted frame that
176		// conflicts with its first arrival is refused even after that
177		// sequence was delivered and left held.

180		held   map[muxSeq]inboundFrame
181		finEOF []bool

199	// NewMux wraps rel in a multiplexing session. Write state in
200	// cfg.StateDir is consulted when present: a fresh directory starts
201	// every channel at sequence 0, while a directory left by a crashed or
202	// restarted process resumes from the earliest confirmed per-channel
203	// positions held by its checkpoints and journal.
204	//
205	// A truncated journal or a flipped bit in a complete record fails
206	// recovery with ErrChecksum rather than replaying unverified frames.
207	func NewMux(rel *ReliableSession, cfg MuxConfig) (*Mux, error) {
208		if cfg.Channels <= 0 {
209			return nil, errors.New("codec: mux channel count must be positive")
210		}
211		if cfg.Window <= 0 {
212			return nil, errors.New("codec: mux window must be positive")
213		}
214		if cfg.StateDir == "" {
215			return nil, errors.New("codec: mux session requires a state directory")
216		}
217		if err := os.MkdirAll(cfg.StateDir, 0o755); err != nil {
218			return nil, err

221		m := &Mux{
222			rel: rel,
223			cfg: cfg,
224			sc:  make([]sendChannel, cfg.Channels),
225			// At most Channels*Window deliveries (one per in-flight frame)
226			// can be awaiting an ack send at once, so the queue is bounded by
227			// the same total buffer bound and a progress-bearing signal is
228			// never dropped; duplicate arrivals beyond it are coalesced
229			// away because acks are cumulative.
230			bases:   make([]uint32, cfg.Channels),
231			seen:    make(map[muxSeq]inboundFrame),
232			held:    make(map[muxSeq]inboundFrame),
233			finEOF:  make([]bool, cfg.Channels),

239		// Load the strict shared journal first, then reconcile per-channel
240		// positions against the checkpoints.
241		var err error
242		m.log, err = openMuxLog(cfg.StateDir)
243		if err != nil {
244			return nil, err
245		}
246	
247		// Per-channel bookkeeping derived strictly from the journal: lowest
248		// and one-past-highest sequence, whether a FIN was seen, and strict
249		// contiguity (a gap or a duplicate would mean a skipped or doubled
250		// frame, which recovery must never silently replay).
251		type span struct {
252			min, max uint32
253			have     bool
254			fin      bool
255		}
256		spans := make([]span, cfg.Channels)
257		for _, rec := range m.log.recs {
258			if int(rec.ch) >= cfg.Channels {
259				return nil, fmt.Errorf("codec: mux journal carries channel %d beyond %d: %w",
260					rec.ch, cfg.Channels-1, ErrChecksum)
261			}
262			sp := &spans[rec.ch]
263			if sp.have {
264				if rec.seq != sp.max+1 {
265					return nil, fmt.Errorf(
266						"codec: mux journal ch %d not contiguous (seq %d after %d): %w",
267						rec.ch, rec.seq, sp.max, ErrChecksum)
268				}
269				if sp.fin {
270					return nil, fmt.Errorf(
271						"codec: mux journal ch %d has frame seq %d after FIN: %w",
272						rec.ch, rec.seq, ErrChecksum)
273				}
274			}
275			if !sp.have {
276				sp.min, sp.have = rec.seq, true
277			}
278			sp.max = rec.seq
279			if rec.fin {
280				sp.fin = true
281			}
282		}
283	
284		for ch := 0; ch < cfg.Channels; ch++ {
285			cpAck, err := loadMuxCheckpoint(cfg.StateDir, uint16(ch))
286			if err != nil {
287				return nil, err
288			}
289			c := &m.sc[ch]
290			sp := spans[ch]
291			switch {
292			case !sp.have:
293				// Nothing left to replay: resume numbering at the confirmed
294				// position; earlier sequences already reached the peer.
295				c.acked, c.next = cpAck, cpAck
296			case cpAck >= sp.max+1:
297				// Checkpoint at/beyond the journal tail.
298				c.acked, c.next = cpAck, cpAck
299			default:
300				// The journal reaches further back than the checkpoint (a
301				// crash between checkpoint and prefix). Resume at the
302				// EARLIER position: the overlap is resent and the receiver
303				// deduplicates it; starting later would skip an
304				// unacknowledged frame.
305				c.acked, c.next = sp.min, sp.max+1
306			}
307			// A FIN record closes the channel; even after its prefix was
308			// discarded the durable close marker keeps it closed.
309			closedByMarker, err := muxChannelClosed(cfg.StateDir, uint16(ch))
310			if err != nil {
311				return nil, err
312			}
313			if sp.have {
314				c.open = true
315				c.closed = sp.fin || closedByMarker
316			} else if closedByMarker {
317				c.open = true
318				c.closed = true
319			}
320		}

322		// The send queue is the journal in arrival order, minus frames
323		// already at/behind their channel's resumed position; it feeds
324		// round-robin Flush and bounds in-flight accounting.
325		m.queue = make([]*queuedFrame, 0, len(m.log.recs))
326		for i := range m.log.recs {
327			rec := m.log.recs[i]

336		return m, nil
337	}
